def objects(g):

    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(x for row in g for x in row)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    for r in range(h):

def find_snake(objs):
    # largest object that is a 1-wide path with exactly one turn (L)
    def is_L(comp):
        cells=set(comp)
        # 1-wide: every cell has <=2 neighbors, path: endpoints have 1
        deg={}
        for (r,c) in comp:
            d=sum(((r+dr,c+dc) in cells) for dr,dc in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)))
            deg[(r,c)]=d
        if max(deg.values())>2: return False
        ends=[p for p,v in deg.items() if v==1]
        if len(ends)!=2: return False
        # exactly one turn: walk path
        import collections
        start=ends[0]; prev=None; cur=start; turns=0; direction=None
        while True:
            nbs=[p for p in ((cur[0]+1,cur[1]),(cur[0]-1,cur[1]),(cur[0],cur[1]+1),(cur[0],cur[1]-1)) if p in cells and p!=prev]
            if not nbs: break
            nxt=nbs[0]
            d=(nxt[0]-cur[0],nxt[1]-cur[1])
            if direction is None: direction=d
            elif d!=direction: turns+=1; direction=d
            if turns>1: return False
            prev,cur=cur,nxt
            if cur==ends[1]: break
        return True
    Ls=[(len(c),col,c) for col,c in objs if is_L(c)]
    if not Ls: return None
    Ls.sort(reverse=True)
    return Ls[0]

def solve(g):
    bg,objs=objects(g)
